title: From the Editor — The Edge of the Sunfields
settingText: A lonely relay settlement where several roads cross under vast Sunfields sky. One shaded table and an empty chair sit conspicuously beneath a patched awning, with the road stretching toward the horizon. No identifiable waiting character.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 4. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: By now, coincidence has developed timing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A town heard one thing. A camp expected another. Somewhere between them, a preacher began arriving before Brandon did.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That changes the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Rumors wander.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Appointments don’t.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There is a relay settlement near the edge of the Sunfields where roads cross and grudges wait in the shade.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Someone there has chosen a chair.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Someone has chosen a day.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And someone is very sure Brandon Mack is late.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

title: The Relay
summary: The trio reaches a crowded relay settlement where routes, messages and travelers overlap. Eva is looking for Samuel; Jessie is looking for supplies; Brandon is looking for a meal.

panelPlan.text: Wide public relay beneath an old tower: patched shade, message boards, communal tables, sleeping travelers, worn equipment housings and people moving through without ceremony.
Eva scans coats and faces for the preacher Isabella described.
Jessie heads toward a parts counter. Brandon follows the smell of food.
A conspicuously refined man at a prepared table notices Brandon before Brandon notices him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: If Samuel came through here, somebody will remember him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Find him after we find fuel and a belt that isn't held together by wire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm adding lunch to the list.

title: The Man Waiting
summary: Ray Silvestro stands from a table laid for two and greets Brandon as the Surveyor. Eva and Jessie recognize the shape of the setup before Brandon answers.

panelPlan.text: Ray rises from a shaded table with two cups, a sealed letter and an old brass token arranged with deliberate precision.
His ornate weathered coat, red neckcloth and refined sidearm distinguish him sharply from Brandon.
Eva and Jessie exchange a look that says this is happening again.
Brandon notices their look first, then turns toward Ray.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You finally came.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm not your Surveyor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You brought a child.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Nobody brought me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: We can establish that part later.

title: A Table for Two
summary: Ray treats Brandon's arrival as a scheduled appointment and refuses to let a denial change the terms. Brandon sits only because Ray's grievance is clearly headed toward confrontation in a crowded public room.

panelPlan.text: Ray gestures to the second chair. Brandon initially remains standing while travelers navigate around the tableau.
Ray notes that he has waited since morning because he was told the Surveyor would arrive today.
Eva stays within earshot rather than pretending this is private.
Brandon finally sits, keeping his hands away from Ray's letter and sidearm.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You came all this way to stand?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I came because the road comes through here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: The preacher said you would arrive today.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did he give you a name?

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: Samuel Hayes.

title: The Surveyor's Debt
summary: Ray explains why he wants the Surveyor: years ago a route survey was sold to raiders, costing Ray's crew people and cargo. He believes the Surveyor personally profited from the betrayal.

panelPlan.text: Ray rotates the brass token between two fingers while describing a convoy route through a narrow cut years earlier.
He does not perform grief broadly; the specificity of names, cargo and distances makes the grievance personal.
Brandon asks what evidence connects the Surveyor to the betrayal besides the route being compromised.
Ray produces the sealed letter Samuel gave him rather than answering from memory.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: Six wagons went through Kestrel Cut. Two came out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: Only three people had the revised route. One of them was the Surveyor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: And you know which of the three sold it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: I know which one vanished with money afterward.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then you have a grievance with that man. Not with me.

title: The Letter
summary: Ray's letter contains a description of Brandon detailed enough to make coincidence less comfortable: coat, hair, stance and habit of watching exits.

panelPlan.text: Ray opens the letter enough for Brandon and Eva to see the handwriting is not his.
The description includes dark coat, black shoulder-length hair, lean build and a tendency to choose seats with sight of the door.
Brandon looks at the crowded relay and points out how many travelers share several of those features.
Eva isolates the behavioral detail as harder to explain by appearance alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: He described you before I ever saw you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: He described a dark-haired man in a coat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He also said you'd sit where you could see the door.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: So would anybody who has eaten in enough crowded rooms.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You have an answer ready for everything except my dead.

title: What Samuel Promised
summary: Eva turns the confrontation toward Samuel's role. Ray says Samuel promised no proof, only that the Surveyor would come and that Ray would finally be able to ask the question himself.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks Ray to repeat Samuel's words as closely as he can rather than summarize them.
Ray dislikes the interrogation but answers because he wants Brandon to hear the promise.
Samuel told Ray the man might deny the title and urged him to ask about Kestrel Cut directly.
Brandon realizes the encounter was designed to provoke knowledge, not merely recognition.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What did Samuel tell you to ask?

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: Kestrel Cut. The revised route. The fourth marker.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I don't know any of those.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: He said you might say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He built the denial into the test again.

title: The Fourth Marker
summary: Ray presses Brandon with the one detail he believes the Surveyor cannot fake ignorance about. Brandon's blank response frustrates Ray because it gives him neither confession nor useful contradiction.

panelPlan.text: Ray places the brass token over a rough route sketch and marks the fourth survey point.
He asks Brandon what stood there before the route was revised. Brandon studies the map honestly and cannot answer.
Eva watches for recognition and sees none she can distinguish from concentration.
Ray's composure slips for the first time because the test produces nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: What stood at the fourth marker?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I don't know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You surveyed it for six weeks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: The Surveyor did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: Stop separating yourself from the man in front of me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That's the only useful distinction I have.

title: No Confession
summary: Ray's disappointment sharpens toward violence, but Brandon refuses both a false confession and a theatrical duel. Jessie interrupts the escalation by naming what Samuel actually arranged: an audience, not an answer.

panelPlan.text: Ray's hand settles near his refined sidearm, not drawing but making the possibility explicit.
Brandon remains seated and does not mirror the gesture.
Jessie returns from the parts counter, takes in the room and places herself where Ray has to see a second person affected by any shot.
She tells Ray Samuel delivered Brandon to his grievance, not the truth about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: I was promised a confession.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then somebody promised you something that wasn't theirs to give.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Samuel arranged a meeting. He didn't prove who was sitting in the chair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You expect me to let him walk away?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I expect you to decide whether killing the wrong man would improve your day.

title: Looking for Samuel
summary: With Ray contained but unresolved, Eva and Jessie search the relay for Samuel while Ray remains near Brandon rather than being allowed to dictate the search.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks relay workers about a weathered preacher in a faded coat. Several remember him because he helped with an argument in a side room.
Jessie learns he has not left the settlement; he is still tending to a family after a child was hurt.
Ray insists on coming. Jessie tells him he can stay where Brandon can see him.
Eva heads toward the side rooms alone while Jessie keeps the public-room situation stable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Worker
dialogueInline.text: Preacher's still here. Side room by the tower stairs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: How long has he been here?

dialogueInline.speaker: Worker
dialogueInline.text: Two days.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Ray, stay with the table.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You think I need supervision.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I think everyone in this room does right now.

title: The Preacher
summary: Eva finds Samuel in a crowded side room bandaging a child's scraped hand and calming adults who are more frightened than the injury warrants.

panelPlan.text: Eva follows the description into a side room and finds Samuel crouched at a bench wrapping a boy's palm.
Two adults argue about whose negligence caused the fall. Samuel keeps attention on the boy rather than adjudicating blame.
Eva recognizes the sun-faded coat Isabella described.
Samuel notices Eva watching but finishes tying the bandage before addressing her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Isabella Torres remembers you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Give me until the bandage is done.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Who is Isabella?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Someone I owe a better conversation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You owe several.

title: Finish the Bandage
summary: Samuel's care for the family is genuine, complicating Eva's desire to reduce him to a simple con man. Jessie arrives and waits until the child is settled before pressing him.

panelPlan.text: Samuel has the boy flex his fingers and checks circulation before releasing the hand.
He redirects the adults from blaming each other toward fixing the loose stair board that caused the fall.
Jessie arrives, sees the situation and waits against the wall rather than interrupting.
Once the family leaves, Samuel washes blood and dust from his hands and turns to them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: The board is still loose. Fix that before deciding whose fault it was.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You make it difficult to decide what kind of man you are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Most people do, up close.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Tell us why you sent Ray after Brandon.

title: Isabella's Name
summary: Eva uses Isabella's message to prove Samuel cannot pretend the Mirage was an innocent conversation. Samuel admits he primed Isabella to expect Merritt, but insists he did not originate the resemblance story.

panelPlan.text: Eva delivers Isabella's exact message: she remembers Samuel's face and does not want him using hers again.
Samuel accepts the rebuke without pretending he merely repeated gossip.
He says Merritt was already a story at the Mirage before he arrived; he learned it from a traveler, then deliberately amplified it.
Jessie asks why he would do that to a woman carrying an old grievance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Isabella said not to use her again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: She's right.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Did you start the Merritt story?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: No. I found it and pushed it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Why?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Because Raina needed to know whether any name would make Brandon reveal something he shouldn't know.

title: Route Notes
summary: Samuel produces practical route notes showing how he and Raina turned real unresolved identities into controlled pressure points along Brandon's likely route.

panelPlan.text: Outside the side room, Samuel opens a route notebook containing dates, names, settlement notes and marks beside places he visited.
Entries include Brannock, General Diaz, Merritt and the Surveyor, but the marks beside them differ.
Eva sees that the operation is mundane: roads, conversations, dates and human wounds rather than hidden technology.
Jessie asks who selected the names. Samuel says Raina did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Raina collected identities with unfinished business and routes Brandon might cross.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then you arrived first and made people expect him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: When I could.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You turned communities into traps.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Tests. That word does not make it kinder.

title: Brannock and Diaz
summary: Samuel distinguishes the first two cases. Brannock happened without him and drew Raina's attention; General Diaz was the first identity they deliberately planted.

panelPlan.text: Eva points to Brannock first. Samuel's note shows a later date than the Last Drop incident.
Samuel explains that Raina heard the Brannock story after it had already spread beyond the settlement.
The Diaz note is different: Samuel visited Cinder Basin first, learned the unresolved succession problem and predicted Diaz's return.
Eva realizes Cinder Basin was an experiment built in response to the accidental Last Drop case.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Brannock?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Not ours. Raina found Brandon because of that story.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Diaz?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: That one was deliberate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You built Cinder Basin after the accident gave you the idea.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Raina had the idea. I knew how to place it.

title: Surveyor and Merritt
summary: The Surveyor was another deliberate test. Merritt was not: a traveler had already reported Brandon's resemblance to Merritt before Samuel reached the Mirage.

panelPlan.text: Samuel points to the Surveyor entry and admits he gave Ray Brandon's description and expected arrival window.
The Merritt entry includes a source note predating Samuel's visit: a traveler from the Mirage who mentioned a man on the road resembling the missing Merritt.
Samuel explains that he went to Isabella because the resemblance story already existed and seemed useful to Raina's theory.
Jessie closes the notebook halfway when she understands what that means.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: The Surveyor was yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Mine and Raina's.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Merritt?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Already a story before I got there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then your operation didn't create the pattern.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: It created some of the encounters. That is not the same thing.

title: The Wounds on Purpose
summary: Samuel admits that he chose people whose unresolved grief or anger would create pressure strong enough to expose a hidden identity if Brandon had one.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks why the tests needed real grievances rather than harmless recognition.
Samuel explains that a liar can deny a name; it is harder to fake ignorance when confronted with specific people, places and consequences.
Jessie points out that the method required hurting people who had not consented to be part of it.
Samuel does not defend the ethics, only the reasoning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You could have tested him with a harmless name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: A harmless name only tests whether he recognizes a word.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: So you chose wounds on purpose.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then you knew exactly what you were spending.

title: Raina Arrives
summary: Raina enters the relay as Samuel's role is exposed. Brandon understands immediately that the investigator from Cinder Basin is the architect behind the later tests.

panelPlan.text: Raina enters the public room from the opposite door carrying dust and road fatigue, not dramatic menace.
She sees Samuel's notebook open in Eva's hands and knows the conversation has already happened.
Ray remains at the table, furious to learn his grievance was selected as leverage.
Brandon looks from Samuel to Raina and finally has a human explanation for at least part of the road behind him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I thought one of the names would catch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Catch what?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Something you knew. A place, a person, a lie you'd practiced.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You used me to test him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I did.

title: Raina's Method
summary: Raina explains how Brannock changed her investigation: an ordinary near-name mistake fit Brandon's appearance and behavior well enough that she assumed a concealed human identity must explain it.

panelPlan.text: Raina lays her own earlier notebook beside Samuel's route notes.
Her first Brandon entry is dated after the Last Drop and records the Brannock story as a rumor she initially believed was evidence of an alias.
She then gathered unresolved names with superficial or reported resemblance and sent Samuel ahead to create controlled confrontations.
Brandon asks why failure did not end the experiment sooner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Brannock looked like the first crack in a false name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It was somebody mishearing Jessie.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I learned that later.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: And instead of stopping, you built better tests.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I thought the mistake had pointed at a real lie by accident.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: How many failures did you need before Brandon became possible?

title: Ray Was Not Evidence
summary: Ray refuses to let Raina turn the failure of her test into another data point. His grievance still belongs to him and the real Surveyor, whoever that man was.

panelPlan.text: Ray takes his sealed letter back from the table and folds the route sketch away.
He tells Raina that learning Brandon is probably not the Surveyor does not make the manipulation harmless.
Raina apologizes without claiming necessity or success.
Ray tells Brandon he no longer has grounds to keep him at the table, but does not offer friendship or absolution.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: My dead were not evidence for your theory.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I don't have a good excuse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: Then don't give me one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Are we finished?

dialogueInline.speaker: Ray
dialogueInline.text: You and I are. The Surveyor and I are not.

title: Did It Work
summary: Brandon asks the question that strips away the rationale for the operation: after Brannock, Diaz, Merritt and the Surveyor, did Raina actually learn that any of those men were him.

panelPlan.text: The immediate conflict has cooled. The five stand around the abandoned prepared table while ordinary relay traffic resumes around them.
Brandon asks Raina whether any test produced knowledge only the assigned man should have.
Raina reviews the names and cannot identify one.
She states the narrow conclusion she can defend: Brandon is the only name that has survived contact with the facts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Did you learn anything?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: None of the other names held up.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Do you believe me now?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I believe Brandon is the only name that held up.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You could have started there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I know that now.

title: The One She Didn't Plant
summary: Eva reconstructs the chronology and finds the problem inside the explanation: Brannock predated Raina, and Merritt's resemblance story predated Samuel's intervention.

panelPlan.text: Eva lays the two notebooks side by side and walks through the names in order rather than treating them as one category.
Brannock: accidental Last Drop mishearing before Raina. Diaz: planted. Surveyor: planted. Merritt: preexisting resemblance story amplified by Samuel.
Samuel confirms the distinctions without minimizing his role.
Raina sees that her conspiracy explains appointments but not the two events that motivated it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Brannock happened before you knew him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Correct.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Diaz and the Surveyor were yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: They were.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Merritt was already there before Samuel arrived.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Which means our explanation starts after the pattern does.

title: The Edge of the Sunfields
summary: The trio leaves the relay with a real answer that only makes the larger question cleaner. Raina and Samuel remain behind, no longer credible as the sole cause of the pattern.

panelPlan.text: Brandon, Eva and Jessie walk toward the rig while Ray stays inside the relay with his own unfinished business.
Raina and Samuel remain beneath the tower, separated from the trio by ordinary distance and consequence.
Eva closes the notebook on the human conspiracy without crossing out Brannock or Merritt.
Final wide panel: the rig heads into late Sunfields light. A distant physical Sunforge remnant catches light beside the road; nobody treats it as an answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We found the people arranging some of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Some is doing a lot of work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then we still don't know who started it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Or whether anyone did.

title: Next: THE USEFUL LIE
settingText: Bellweather in rain at night: porch light, covered wake table, several empty chairs, and one especially conspicuous empty place near the end. No people shown clearly.
summary: Art-directed closing teaser splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 4. Point directly at the next loaded pressure without revealing its resolution.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Raina rigged some of the encounters.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Samuel planted the expectation.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Mystery solved.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Except Brannock happened without them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So did Merritt.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They found the hand on the scale.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They still don’t know what put the scale there.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And one last planted name is already waiting at a wake.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: THE USEFUL LIE
